claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute financially towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! Just one more question to ensure I have all the information:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation, or does he live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex is currently in hospital. He's in hospital abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. That's important information as it may affect your eligibility. I need to understand the situation better:

**How long has Alex been in hospital abroad, and what was the reason he went abroad - was it specifically to receive hospital treatment, or were you living abroad when he was hospitalized?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure about all the details to be honest. He is in hospital abroad, but I can't say for certain whether we only went abroad specifically for him to be in hospital or what the exact situation was with that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - thank you for being honest about what you know and don't know.

Let me ask this: **Are you currently back in the UK yourself, and are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about those details either, to be honest. I know he's in hospital abroad, but I can't say for certain whether I'm back in the UK or whether I'm regularly spending money on him while he's there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being upfront about the uncertainty around these details. Let me ask one more clarifying question:

**Do you know approximately how long Alex has been in hospital abroad - is it less than 12 weeks, more than 12 weeks, or are you unsure of the timeframe?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm afraid I don't know the timeframe - I'm unsure how long he's been in hospital abroad.

**Assessment Summary for Alex:**

I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. Here's why:

Under normal circumstances, you would qualify for Child Benefit because:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live in the UK
- Alex normally lives with you
- No one else is claiming for him

**However**, because Alex is currently in hospital abroad, special rules apply that could affect your eligibility:

1. There is generally a **12-week time limit** for children in hospital
2. There are **exceptions** that might allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit if:
   - Alex only went abroad to be in hospital (not for other reasons), AND
   - You are back in the UK and regularly spending money on him

Since you don't have information about:
- How long Alex has been in hospital
- Whether he went abroad specifically for hospital treatment
- Whether you're currently back in the UK
- Whether you're regularly spending money on him while he's there

I cannot determine if you're eligible, ineligible, or if the exceptions apply.

**My recommendation:** Contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office directly with the details of your situation. They can help you understand how these specific rules apply to your circumstances once you have more information about the details of Alex's hospital stay abroad.
